purpose: Part of the final 69 catalog titles, group 2 of 4, live CSM research, nums 958-974.

contentFlagModel.mappingNote: This research preserves CSM's current visible category label and proposes the nearest app level. Production catalog edits should be made only by the follow-up importer/reviewer.

entries.title: The Flintstones

violence.summary: Cartoonish slapstick violence imitates the original cartoon, including Bam Bam clubbing Barney in the head, plus a kidnapping and threat against Pebbles and Bam Bam by the villain.

language.summary: Mild language includes words like "damn" and "sucks."

romance.summary: Fred flirts with his secretary, whose dialogue includes sexually-charged one-liners like "use me how you see fit."

drinking.summary: A character smokes a prehistoric cigarette, and Fred drinks and comes home drunk in one scene, with his mother-in-law accusing him of drunkenness.

handoffNotes: Kidnapping and threat against two children may need light prose context for younger viewers.

entries.title: Jingle All the Way

violence.summary: Constant slapstick violence includes brawling, fake-choking, macing in the eyes, trampling, falling from heights, getting tasered and kicked in the crotch, plus comic explosions and boomerang gags on a TV screen.

language.summary: One-off mild words like "damn," "loser," "goofy-butt," "simpleton," and "shut up," plus a racially insensitive joke comparing sweating to "a dog in a Chinese restaurant."

romance.summary: Complaints about infidelity, innuendo like "I've got just the tool for the job," an attempted seduction of a married character, spousal kissing, and a non-sexual undershirt-and-boxers scene.

drinking.summary: Adults drink occasionally, including spiking coffee at a diner and swigging liquor bottles; a fantasy sequence shows a young child drinking from a liquor bottle, plus brief cigar smoking.

handoffNotes: The racially insensitive joke about a 'dog in a Chinese restaurant' should be preserved in sensitivity review even though the overall language level is low.

entries.title: Sister Act

violence.summary: The heroine witnesses her mobster boyfriend order henchmen to shoot and kill someone, is later pursued and shot at, and is abducted at gunpoint before escaping unharmed.

language.summary: Occasional profanity includes "s--t" and "hell," plus a strongly sarcastic blessing that implies the f-word.

romance.summary: Some kissing and mild mentions of sex occur.

drinking.summary: Some references to alcohol, casino-setting smoking, and champagne drinking are shown.

handoffNotes: The heroine witnessing an ordered killing and being pursued/abducted at gunpoint may need prose context for younger viewers, despite the moderate violence category label.

entries.title: Sister Act 2: Back in the Habit

violence.summary: The sequel is crime-free and villain-free, with no violence or scary content depicted.

language.summary: Infrequent mild language includes "hell," "ass," "crap," and "Jesus Christ."

romance.summary: No sexual content or nudity is depicted.

violence.summary: Kris bops Sawyer on the head for mistreating Albert; otherwise the film is largely nonviolent.

language.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful language concern.

romance.summary: A couple in a relationship hugs, shares one kiss, and talks about their future as a married couple.

drinking.summary: Characters smoke cigars and cigarettes, and in two scenes characters appear drunk.

entries.title: North
entries.researchBasis: live CSM search (no review found) plus Wikipedia fallback by researcher

violence.summary: No CSM review exists. Per Wikipedia, violence is minimal: an assassination attempt at an airport is interrupted before impact, and an Alaskan segment references a cultural senicide practice (elderly sent out to sea) treated matter-of-factly rather than graphically.

language.summary: No CSM review exists and no language/profanity detail is available from the Wikipedia fallback source.

romance.summary: No CSM review exists and no romance/sexual content detail is available from the Wikipedia fallback source.

drinking.summary: No CSM review exists and no drinking/drugs/smoking detail is available from the Wikipedia fallback source.

handoffNotes: No live CSM review exists for this title (commonsensemedia.org/movie-reviews/north 404s and is actually a 'North of North' TV review / 'North by Northwest' review, not this film) -- catalog's currentCa of '8+' is NOT sourced from a real CSM page. Flag for reviewer: this title should likely carry a 'Not on CSM; substitute source used' style note rather than an unqualified '8+', since that field currently implies live CSM backing it does not have.

Grief/loss theme: the plot centers on a child's feeling of parental estrangement/rejection and a fantasy divorce from his parents; the Alaska segment depicts a senicide (elderly sent to sea to die) practice, referenced matter-of-factly. Also references a character's death in the Texas section. Recommend prose context given the separation/death themes, per instructions to call these out explicitly.

violence.summary: Lots of comic crashes and falls, plus repeated fight scenes with shooting, explosions, and swords between soldiers/warriors, with no visible lasting injuries except charring; dinosaur-skeleton and Attila the Hun chase scenes may startle younger viewers though encounters stay cartoonish.

language.summary: Mild profanity such as "don't be a kiss-ass" and "screwed up," name-calling like "weirdy" and "cupcake," and occasional religious exclamations like "Oh my God."

romance.summary: Only mild flirting, plus one scene where a character views a woman through binoculars and a bystander asks if he's "checking her out."

drinking.summary: Minimal substance use limited to one scene of an adult drinking a glass of wine.

entries.title: Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian

violence.summary: Characters are frequently chased and threatened with weapons like spears and swords, though no serious injuries occur; a giant octopus causes havoc and creepy Egyptian underworld imagery may frighten younger viewers.

language.summary: Mild profanity including words like "dammit" and "suck," plus some older slang expressions; overall language usage remains minimal.

romance.summary: Flirting and kissing between characters, with a couple of innuendos likely to go unnoticed by children; some statues appear unclothed but nothing explicit is displayed.

drinking.summary: No drinking, drugs, or smoking depicted.

handoffNotes: A CSM movie review does genuinely exist for this sequel (distinct from the CSM game review of the same title) -- confirmed by fetching the actual movie-reviews page, not just relying on search snippets.

entries.title: The Polar Express

violence.summary: Continuous close calls include fast-moving train/pneumatic-tube rides shown from a child's POV, treacherous climbs atop the train, falls, lost kids, a runaway railway car, and cracking ice under a speeding train; a villain uses a creepy puppet to frighten the protagonist in a dark chamber filled with broken talking dolls.

language.summary: No language concerns noted by CSM.

romance.summary: No sexual content or romance noted by CSM.

drinking.summary: No drinking, drugs, or smoking depicted.

handoffNotes: CSM parent/kid reviews flag divided opinions about the film's unsettling animation style and dark-chamber sequence with a menacing conductor/hobo-style character as scarier than the G rating suggests -- worth noting alongside the 'some' violence/scariness category label for younger viewers.

entries.title: Curious George

violence.summary: CSM labels this category 'not present'; the page's own descriptive text still notes slapstick falls/jumps and monkey antics (painting on walls, stealing and flying off on balloons, King-Kong-style scale gag), all comedic in tone.

language.summary: No language concerns noted by CSM.

romance.summary: CSM labels this category 'not present'; the page's own descriptive text notes some flirting between Ted and Maggie and a kiss at the end.

drinking.summary: No drinking, drugs, or smoking depicted.

handoffNotes: CSM's own category labels read 'Not present' for violence and romance despite descriptive text mentioning slapstick antics and a Ted/Maggie flirtation-and-kiss subplot -- preserved CSM's literal label per protocol, but flagging the discrepancy for reviewer awareness.

CSM also separately notes an emotionally-intense scene where George is taken away by animal control at the Man in the Yellow Hat's request, plus unpunished fraud by a human character (Ted) -- worth light handoff context though it doesn't map cleanly to the four tracked flags.

entries.title: Happy Feet

violence.summary: Penguins are attacked by scary leopard seals and face cold/blizzards; additional peril includes seabirds threatening Mumble, killer whales pursuing penguins, and an upsetting zoo hallucination scene.

language.summary: Mild profanity including "freakin'" and phrases like "shut up," "fatty," and "idiot," plus a reference to buttocks humor.

romance.summary: Suggestive penguin mating behavior runs throughout, with flirtatious dialogue and references to attraction; female penguin designs emphasize physical features and there are objectifying comments among male characters.

drinking.summary: No drinking, drugs, or smoking depicted.

handoffNotes: CSM's review also flags racial/ethnic stereotyping as a notable concern -- smaller penguins coded as Latino and portrayed as party-loving, a larger penguin coded as Black and portrayed as an oversexed, fundamentalist preacher -- worth surfacing to reviewers even though it doesn't map to the four tracked flags.

entries.title: Happy Feet Two

violence.summary: An iceberg traps the penguins in a snow valley they can't climb out of, and situations appear dire; also krill being consumed by larger sea creatures, an elephant seal threatening characters, seal combat, and predatory birds attacking penguin chicks.

romance.summary: Penguin parents embrace affectionately; one character makes a suggestive remark toward another ("You, me, egg, now!"), and flirtation occurs throughout.

drinking.summary: No drinking, drugs, or smoking depicted.

handoffNotes: Verified a genuine CSM movie review exists specifically for this sequel (distinct from the CSM app reviews of the same title, e.g. 'Happy Feet Two: Erik's Adventure') by fetching the actual movie-reviews page rather than relying on search snippets.

entries.title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars

violence.summary: Constant but bloodless animated sci-fi action, including lightsaber duels and small-arms/artillery energy-beam fire.

romance.summary: Alien dancing girls perform in tight clothing, and there are some longing glances.

drinking.summary: In an outer-space nightclub, several non-humans drink what are presumably intoxicants, and a huge slug-like alien smokes from a hookah.

handoffNotes: Confirmed via live fetch that this CSM page is for the 2008 animated CGI film 'Star Wars: The Clone Wars' (distinct from the separate CSM TV review for the 'Clone Wars' animated series and the CSM page for the earlier 2003 Genndy Tartakovsky 'Star Wars: Clone Wars' micro-series).

entries.title: Corpse Bride

violence.summary: Some scariness including crows in trees, talking skeletons, and dead bodies with rotting flesh and maggots (the corpse bride's eye occasionally pops out to reveal a talking maggot living inside her, who offers romantic advice), all played for gothic/comic effect rather than horror.

language.summary: CSM labels this category 'None'; the page's own text notes "some spicy sayings but nothing too out of line."

romance.summary: No sexual content or nudity noted; the central story is a quirky, PG-appropriate arranged-marriage fairy tale about love and selflessness.

drinking.summary: CSM labels this category 'None'; the page's own text notes "the skeletons drink, but it's clearly fantasy."

handoffNotes: Death/decay theme throughout: the film is a comic-gothic fairy tale about an arranged marriage that accidentally binds the hero to a dead woman, with skeletons, rotting corpses, and an afterlife setting played for whimsy rather than genuine grief -- worth noting given the death imagery even though it is not framed as loss/grief in the traditional sense.

entries.title: ParaNorman

violence.summary: Dark, eerie tone with grotesque spirit imagery (flayed skin, severed necks, exposed intestines), chase sequences, a destructive witch with electric blasts and thorny spikes, armed townspeople, bullying, a witnessed fatal heart attack, and references to an 11-year-old's execution by hanging.

language.summary: Frequent insults like "freak," "stupid," "loser," and "fatty"; "the F-word" is referenced but not said aloud; also "jackass," "damnation," "boobs," "wiener," "hell," and religious exclamations "Jesus"/"God."

romance.summary: A teen character appears shirtless in a towel, another teen makes seduction attempts in midriff-baring clothing with implied butt-grabbing, a casino billboard shows a woman with money in her cleavage, and there's an early reference to "sex and violence" on TV.

drinking.summary: Teens occasionally consume alcohol, and one character takes medication.

handoffNotes: Grief/death theme: the plot involves a boy who can see and speak to the dead, includes witnessing a character's fatal heart attack, and references the historical execution by hanging of an 11-year-old accused of witchcraft. The film's emotional core deals directly with death, guilt, and being haunted by the past -- recommend explicit prose context per grief/loss/death callout guidance.

entries.title: Isle of Dogs

violence.summary: A metal chunk is shown impaled in a boy's head, dog fights are depicted as smoke clouds with animated blood, military-issue teeth fire like bullets, there's a live fish-chopping scene, poisoning, dead bodies, caged dogs, a train wreck mention, canine flu imagery, dog skeletons, a gory kidney transplant, and suicide references.

language.summary: One instance of "son of a bitch," one use of "bitch" (referring to a female dog), and two uses of "damn it."

romance.summary: References to "dogs in heat" and mating, puppy litters mentioned, and a male character's bare bottom shown exiting a bathtub.

drinking.summary: An adult character drinks alcohol at a bar, and a minor character smokes a pipe.

handoffNotes: CSM's violence category explicitly lists 'suicide references' alongside death, dead bodies, and gory imagery (kidney transplant gore, dog skeletons, poisoning) -- this is a notably intense violence profile for an animated film and should carry explicit prose context given the grief/death/darker themes involved.

entries.title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid

violence.summary: A trio of teens bullies and menaces Greg and Rowley, forcing Rowley to do something gross after catching them; Rodrick threatens to kill Greg; a girl taunts, wrestles, and later beats up Greg in front of the whole school.

language.summary: Frequent insults like "dumb," "moron," "stupid," "clueless," "jerk," "tool," "idiot," "freakjob," and "wimp"; a couple uses of "crap" and "God" as an exclamation; "freakin'" a few times; plus scatological references to snot, boogers, and farting.

romance.summary: Rodrick has a fictional skin-mag-style magazine ("Moto Mamas") showing scantily clad women on motorcycles with only the cover shown; a middle-school boy walks hand-in-hand with girls; Greg mentions hearing girls call a boy's butt "cute"; a few quick glimpses of kids on toilets or peeing with no nudity.

drinking.summary: No drinking, drugs, or smoking depicted.

handoffNotes: CSM's live age rating is 9+, slightly above the catalog's current 8+ -- not one of the flagged 'Not on CSM'/'(approximate)' titles, but worth a reviewer's attention as a minor rating drift.
